cases.sentence: – Что ж, было весело? – спросила она, с виноватым и ___ на лице выходя к нему навстречу.
cases.explain: «кротким выражением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Well, was it nice?” she asked, coming out to meet him with a penitent and meek expression.

cases.sentence: – Как обыкновенно, – отвечал он, тотчас же по одному взгляду на нее поняв, что она в одном из своих ___.
cases.explain: «хороших расположений» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Just as usual,” he answered, seeing at a glance that she was in one of her good moods. He was used by now to these transitions, and he was particularly glad to see it today, as he was in a specially good humor himself.

cases.sentence: Он уже привык к этим переходам и нынче был особенно рад ему, потому что сам был в самом ___ духа.
cases.explain: «хорошем расположении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Just as usual,” he answered, seeing at a glance that she was in one of her good moods. He was used by now to these transitions, and he was particularly glad to see it today, as he was in a specially good humor himself.

cases.sentence: Теперь уже не учительница ___, а княжна Сорокина, которая жила в подмосковной деревне вместе с графиней Вронской, представилась Анне.
cases.explain: «шведской королевы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Yes … oh, no, wait a minute! The day after tomorrow’s Sunday, I have to be at maman’s,” said Vronsky, embarrassed, because as soon as he uttered his mother’s name he was aware of her intent, suspicious eyes. His embarrassment confirmed her suspicion. She flushed hotly and drew away from him. It was now not the Queen of Sweden’s swimming-mistress who filled Anna’s imagination, but the young Princess Sorokina. She was staying in a village near Moscow with Countess Vronskaya.

cases.sentence: Теперь уже не учительница шведской королевы, а княжна Сорокина, которая жила в ___ вместе с графиней Вронской, представилась Анне.
cases.explain: «подмосковной деревне» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes … oh, no, wait a minute! The day after tomorrow’s Sunday, I have to be at maman’s,” said Vronsky, embarrassed, because as soon as he uttered his mother’s name he was aware of her intent, suspicious eyes. His embarrassment confirmed her suspicion. She flushed hotly and drew away from him. It was now not the Queen of Sweden’s swimming-mistress who filled Anna’s imagination, but the young Princess Sorokina. She was staying in a village near Moscow with Countess Vronskaya.

cases.sentence: По…стой! – сказал Вронский, не раздвигая ___ бровей, но останавливая ее за руку. – В чем дело?
cases.explain: «мрачной складки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Stop! sto‑op!” said Vronsky, with no change in the gloomy lines of his brows, though he held her by the hand. “What is it all about? I said that we must put off going for three days, and on that you told me I was lying, that I was not an honorable man.”

cases.sentence: Я сказал, что отъезд надо отложить на три дня, ты мне на это сказала, что я лгу, что я ___.
cases.explain: «нечестный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Stop! sto‑op!” said Vronsky, with no change in the gloomy lines of his brows, though he held her by the hand. “What is it all about? I said that we must put off going for three days, and on that you told me I was lying, that I was not an honorable man.”

cases.sentence: – Да, и повторяю, что человек, который попрекает меня, что он всем пожертвовал для меня, – сказала она, вспоминая слова еще прежней ссоры, – что это хуже, чем ___, – это человек без сердца.
cases.explain: «нечестный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, and I repeat that the man who reproaches me with having sacrificed everything for me,” she said, recalling the words of a still earlier quarrel, “that he’s worse than a dishonorable man—he’s a heartless man.”

cases.sentence: «Он ненавидит меня, это ясно», – подумала она и молча, не оглядываясь, ___ вышла из комнаты.
cases.explain: «неверными шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “He hates me, that’s clear,” she thought, and in silence, without looking round, she walked with faltering steps out of the room. “He loves another woman, that’s even clearer,” she said to herself as she went into her own room. “I want love, and there is none. So, then, all is over.” She repeated the words she had said, “and it must be ended.”
